hints.content: The question is asking how many cups of pineapple juice Francine uses for one cup of orange juice. We can answer this question by finding the unit rate, cups of pineapple juice per cup  of orange juice.
To find cups of pineapple juice per cup of orange juice, we divide cups of pineapple juice by cups of orange juice.
$\phantom{=}\dfrac{~~~ \dfrac23 \text{ cup of pineapple juice}~~~}{\dfrac13 \text{ cup of orange juice}}$

options.explanation: We rewrote the complex fraction as a division problem because the fraction bar means "divided by".
We changed dividing by $\dfrac13$ to multiplying by $\dfrac31$ because dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.

Here's how we multiplied the fractions:

$\phantom{=}\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac31$

$ =\dfrac{2 \cdot 3}{3\cdot 1}$

$=\dfrac{6}{3}$

hints.content: $ 2$ cups of pineapple juice per cup of orange juice $\qquad$ [[☃ explanation 4]]

options.explanation:
Here's how we simplified the fraction:

$ \phantom{=}\dfrac{6}{3}$

$= \dfrac{2 \cdot \cancel{3}}{1 \cdot \cancel{3}}$

$ = 2$

hints.content: For $1$ cup of orange juice, Francine uses $2$ cups of pineapple juice.
